instagram_caption:
🚴‍♂️ The $4B Rocket That Crashed — and who climbed out alive.

At the start of 2020 Peloton was still a niche startup: 2018 revenue sat around $0.91B and by fiscal 2021 Peloton reported $4.02B in revenue — the pandemic sent at-home fitness into hyperdrive. For a brief moment Peloton looked unstoppable: a private-user economy, hardware plus subscription, and a sky-high public valuation that symbolized the entire work-from-home boom.

Then reality hit. By 2022 Peloton's revenue had pulled back to roughly $3.6B; 2023 fell again to about $3.2B and 2024 landed near $2.5B. The reasons are visible in the data: returns, supply-chain headaches and a saturated hardware market. At the same time legacy fitness-maker Nautilus never rode the rocket — it hovered near $0.9B for years, sliding to about $0.56B by 2024.

The survivors and pivoters are the story’s twists. Lululemon’s long-term apparel growth went from roughly $4.4B in 2020 to around $6.26B in 2021 and surged into an $8–9B runway by 2023–24 after it bought Mirror in 2020 and doubled down on digital+retail synergy. New challengers like Tonal and Echelon show a different shape: slower hardware revenue but growing subscription mixes — Tonal moved from effectively zero in early years to an estimated $0.30B by 2024; Echelon climbed into the low hundreds of millions.

Numbers tell the drama: one firm (Peloton) rocketed from near-zero to $4.02B in three years, then corrected back toward $2.5B — while a retail giant (Lululemon) quietly converted fitness interest into sustained revenue growth, from ~$4.4B (2020) to ~$9.3B (2024). Which strategy wins long-term — hardware-first hype or apparel + subscription ecosystem — is the core tension.

Home Fitness Crash & Comeback — a data-driven look at how the pandemic transformed (and then corrected) the at-home fitness market.

Key points: Peloton’s revenue grew from effectively zero pre-2012 to $4.02B in fiscal 2021 before sliding to about $2.5B by 2024. Nautilus (Bowflex) showed long-term stagnation, holding near $0.9B for years and decreasing to around $0.56B in 2024. Lululemon’s acquisition of Mirror in 2020 and expansion into digital+retail accelerated growth from ~$4.4B (2020) to $9.3B (2024). Newer players Tonal and Echelon represent rising niche segments with estimated revenues reaching the low hundreds of millions by 2024.

This timeline visualizes 20 years (2005–2024) of revenue trajectories to highlight how a single external shock (COVID-19) created winners, losers and long-term pivots. Source material: company filings (Peloton, Nautilus, Lululemon), investor presentations, industry reporting and press releases.
